title: District 1, Ho Chi Minh City: what it's like and renting
description: District 1 for renters: its four new wards, landmarks, metro stations, asking rents by bedroom from the eno.vn Rent Index and what to ask before a viewing.
h1: District 1, Ho Chi Minh City: what living there is like and where to rent
intro: District 1 is the historic centre of Ho Chi Minh City. Since 1 July 2025 it has been split into four official wards: Sai Gon, Ben Thanh, Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh. It is one of the city's dearer places to rent. People, rental ads and the eno.vn Rent Index still call it District 1. On the index's 23 November 2026 snapshot, its median apartment asking rent was about 2.4 times the city-wide apartment median.
keyPoints: Since 1 July 2025, official addresses use four new wards instead of District 1: **Sai Gon, Ben Thanh, Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh** (Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15).
On the eno.vn Rent Index's 23 November 2026 snapshot, District 1's median asking rent was {{vnd:6500000}} a month for a studio and {{vnd:19900000}} a month for a one-bedroom.
On 23 November 2026, District 1 ranked 5th of 21 areas for median apartment asking rent. District 2, District 4, District 9 and District 7 were higher.
Metro Line 1 began commercial service on 22 December 2024. Its three underground stations, Ben Thanh, Opera House and Ba Son, serve the old centre.

Rent ranges in District 1 are wide. On 23 November 2026, the middle half of one-bedroom asking rents ran from {{vnd:12800000}} to {{vnd:31900000}} a month. Filter by bedrooms and sort by price before you shortlist.

sections.title: What is District 1 in Ho Chi Minh like for a first-time renter?

blocks.text: District 1 is the old commercial and administrative centre of Ho Chi Minh City. It has the cathedral, the central post office, City Hall, Ben Thanh Market and the Nguyen Hue pedestrian street, all within walking distance of each other. If you rent there, you trade space and quiet for being close to almost everything, and you pay for it.

Officially, District 1 no longer exists. On 1 July 2025 Vietnam abolished the district level. The National Assembly Standing Committee's [Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/co-cau-to-chuc/resolution-1685-nq-ubtvqh15-2025-reorganization-of-commune-level-administrative-divisions-of-ho-chi-minh-in-2025-403012-d1.html) merged its ten wards into four, and the new wards began operating on 1 July 2025. A lease or utility bill now shows a ward such as **Sai Gon ward** or **Ben Thanh ward**. Taxi drivers, landlords and listings still say "District 1" or "Quận 1".

The housing is mostly apartments: studios and serviced flats in older buildings and alley houses, plus high-end towers. On 23 November 2026, every one of the 203 District 1 listings in the eno.vn Rent Index was an apartment. The index had too few houses or rooms in District 1 to publish a figure for them.

sections.title: Landmarks, streets and everyday conveniences in District 1

blocks.text: Most of what visitors come to Ho Chi Minh City for is in District 1, and so are the city's first metro stations. For a renter, that means short walks to food, shops and transport, along with heavy foot traffic and evening crowds near the main sights.

blocks.caption: District 1 landmarks and their addresses, as listed by Vietnam's national tourism site (vietnam.travel), read on 24 November 2026
rows: Former presidential palace, open to visitors
Nguyen Hue Street and City Hall
Pedestrian street, busiest at sundown. City Hall is not open to the public
Market with food stalls at the far end

blocks.text: Is there a metro station in District 1?

Yes, there are three. According to [JICA](https://www.jica.go.jp/english/information/press/2024/20241225_21.html), which financed the line, Metro Line 1 began commercial operation on 22 December 2024 and runs 19.7 km from Ben Thanh in the city centre to Suoi Tien through 14 stations, three of them on a 2.5 km underground section. VnExpress named those three underground stations in December 2024: **Ben Thanh, Opera House and Ba Son**, all in the old centre. The line runs north-east towards Thu Duc, which helps if you work in that direction. [Getting around Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-around-ho-chi-minh-city) covers buses, Grab and motorbikes.

In November 2024, Viet Nam News reported the city's fare decision. Single trips cost {{vnd:7000-20000}} in cash depending on distance, a one-day pass {{vnd:40000}} and a monthly pass {{vnd:300000}}. Check the fares at the station, because they can change.
What are the four new wards named after?

According to Vietcetera's post-merger guide (July 2025), each new ward takes its name from a local landmark: Ben Thanh Market, the pink Tan Dinh Church and the Ong Lanh Bridge. The old Da Kao neighbourhood, known for its French-era buildings, is now part of Sai Gon ward.

Start with the four wards. They match fairly well how the area feels on the ground. The core around the cathedral and Nguyen Hue is Sai Gon ward. The market and backpacker streets are in Ben Thanh ward. Tan Dinh is to the north and Cau Ong Lanh is to the south along the canal.

blocks.text: On 24 November 2026, the cheaper studios on [eno.vn's District 1 rentals page](/c/rentals/d1) were listed in **Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh wards**. The highest asking prices belonged to named towers such as The Marq, Grand Marina and Vinhomes Golden River. That pattern is a snapshot of one day's listings. Treat it as a starting point and not as a rule.

blocks.title: Two names for every address
blocks.text: A listing may say "District 1, Ben Nghe" while your contract says "Sai Gon ward". Both can describe the same building. Check that the street number and building name match, and read the ward on official papers using the table above.

sections.title: How much is rent in District 1, Ho Chi Minh City?

blocks.text: According to the eno.vn Rent Index, on its 23 November 2026 snapshot District 1's median apartment asking rent was {{vnd:11000000}} a month. The city-wide apartment median was {{vnd:4600000}} a month. The District 1 median is pulled down by its many studios, so the figures by bedroom tell you more.

blocks.caption: District 1 median asking rents by apartment size, eno.vn Rent Index snapshot of 23 November 2026 (asking prices, not signed leases)

blocks.text: On 23 November 2026, District 1 ranked 5th of the index's 21 areas for median apartment asking rent. District 2, District 4, District 9 and District 7 ranked higher, and Binh Tan and Hoc Mon had the lowest medians. The [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) is updated regularly, so check today's figures there. [Rent prices in Ho Chi Minh City by district](/guides/rent-prices) compares the areas side by side.

These are **asking prices**, and the index itself notes that actual rents are often lower after negotiation. The middle half for one-bedrooms is wide, so a building's age and services matter more than the District 1 label.

eno.vn is a classifieds marketplace for expats and locals in Vietnam. Its [District 1 rentals page](/c/rentals/d1) lists the District 1 homes posted there, which you can filter by bedrooms and sort by price. On 24 November 2026 it showed 203 apartments.

items.title: Open the District 1 page
items.text: Go to [District 1 rentals](/c/rentals/d1), or start from [all rentals](/c/rentals) and pick District 1 from the area list.

items.title: Pick a size
items.text: Use the 1 BR, 2 BR or 3+ BR links. Studios appear in the full list.

items.title: Sort by price or date
items.text: Choose Price low → high to find the bottom of the range, or Newest to see listings likely still available. The Map view shows which ward each home is in.

items.title: Read the card
items.text: Each card shows the monthly asking price, the size in m², the ward or building and how long ago the home was listed. Compare the price with the bedroom table above.

items.title: Ask about availability
items.text: The Check availability button asks the eno team to check whether a home is still free. On 24 November 2026 it covered up to five homes at once. Listings marked Official partner come from GoPlus, an official eno.vn partner, which answers in eno.vn chat.

blocks.text: How should I shortlist by price and type?

Set your ceiling first, then decide on the type of home. On 23 November 2026, a typical studio was about a third of the price of a typical one-bedroom. The jump from studio to one-bedroom is the biggest single cost decision you make in District 1. If you mainly want the location, a studio in Tan Dinh or Cau Ong Lanh ward gets you there for much less.
Shortlist four or five homes in the same price band. That way you compare like with like: what the rent includes, the building's age, and the walk to the metro or your work.

sections.title: What should I ask a landlord before a viewing?

blocks.text: Ask about anything that changes the real monthly cost, and get the answer in writing in chat before you travel to a viewing. In central buildings, the gap between the asking rent and what you actually pay usually comes from fees and bills.

items: Is the home still available, and from what date?
Is the advertised price the full monthly rent, and for what minimum term?
What does the rent include: management fee, internet, cleaning, water?
How is electricity charged, per meter reading or at a set rate per unit?
How many months' deposit, and on what terms is it returned? See [rental deposits in Vietnam](/rental-deposit-vietnam).
Is there motorbike or car parking, and does it cost extra?
Are the photos current, and are the furniture and appliances in them included?
Will the landlord make the residence declaration for you? [Renting an apartment as a foreigner](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) explains it.

blocks.text: Do not pay a deposit or "holding fee" for a home you have not seen, and check that the person you pay is the landlord or their authorised agent. Read [eno.vn's safety page](/safety) before you transfer money.

sections.title: Is District 1 a good place to live?

blocks.text: District 1 suits people who want to walk everywhere and are willing to pay for a central address or live in a small space. It suits families who need room, or anyone on a tight budget, less well.

blocks.caption: Trade-offs of renting in District 1
rows: Walk to markets, restaurants, the cathedral and Nguyen Hue
Crowds and late-night noise near the main sights and backpacker streets
The metro runs only towards Thu Duc so far
Space costs a lot more: on 23 November 2026 a typical two-bedroom was over five times a typical studio
Easy for visiting friends to find
Street parking and traffic are hard work at rush hour

blocks.text: If you will work across the city, compare commute times before you sign. [Where to live in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher) compares the other neighbourhoods. [Cost of living in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers) puts rent alongside your other monthly costs.

sections.title: Before you commit to a District 1 rental

blocks.text: Before you sign, make sure the contract matches what you were told in chat. Then visit the home at the time of day you would actually be there.

items: Visit in the evening as well as by day. Noise from bars and the street varies a lot from one building to the next.
Check that the contract states the rent, what it includes, the deposit and the notice period exactly as agreed, and gives the ward under its new name.
Photograph every room and every appliance when you move in, so you can claim your deposit back later.
Plan the move: [Saigon Moving](/guides/saigonmoving) covers moving furniture, and [furnishing a home in Vietnam](/furnishing-a-home-in-vietnam) covers what to buy.

faqs.q: What is District 1 in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: District 1 is the historic centre of Ho Chi Minh City. It is home to Notre Dame Cathedral, the Saigon Central Post Office, Reunification Palace, Nguyen Hue Street and Ben Thanh Market. Since 1 July 2025 it has officially been four wards: Sai Gon, Ben Thanh, Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh. Locals, landlords and rental listings still call the area District 1.

faqs.q: What does HCM mean in Vietnam?
faqs.a: HCM is the usual short form of Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam's largest city, also often called Saigon. Addresses and listings write it as HCM, HCMC or TP.HCM. Since 1 July 2025, Ho Chi Minh City has also included the former provinces of Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau, and it is divided into wards and communes rather than districts.

faqs.q: Does District 1 still exist in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: District 1 no longer exists as an official unit. Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15 merged District 1's ten wards into four (Sai Gon, Ben Thanh, Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh), and the new wards began operating on 1 July 2025. The name District 1 is still used every day by people, taxi drivers and rental listings.

faqs.q: How much is rent in District 1 Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Rent in District 1 depends heavily on size. On the eno.vn Rent Index snapshot of 23 November 2026, District 1's median apartment asking rent was about 2.4 times the city-wide apartment median, and District 1 ranked 5th of 21 areas. A typical one-bedroom cost roughly three times a typical studio. The rent table in this guide gives the figures by bedroom.

faqs.q: Is there a metro station in District 1 Ho Chi Minh?
faqs.a: District 1 has three Metro Line 1 stations: Ben Thanh, Opera House and Ba Son, the line's three underground stations. Metro Line 1 began commercial service on 22 December 2024 and runs 19.7 km from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien through 14 stations, heading north-east towards Thu Duc. Fares depend on distance, and day and monthly passes are available.

faqs.q: Which part of District 1 is cheapest to rent in?
faqs.a: On 24 November 2026, the cheapest studios on eno.vn's District 1 rentals page were in Tan Dinh and Cau Ong Lanh wards. The highest asking prices were in named high-end towers. Listings change daily, so sort the District 1 page by price and check the eno.vn Rent Index before deciding.

faqs.q: Is District 1 a good place to live in Ho Chi Minh?
faqs.a: District 1 is a good place to live if you want to walk to restaurants, markets and the metro and accept higher rent for the space you get. Living there also means crowds and late-night noise near the main sights and backpacker streets. Families needing several bedrooms, and renters on a tight budget, often find better value in other neighbourhoods.
